title: Cross-Family Linear-Probe Transfer Benchmark for Jailbreak Detection

original_idea.body:
# Cross-Family Linear-Probe Transfer Benchmark for Jailbreak Detection

**Problem:** Activation-probe jailbreak detectors are cheap and effective, but it is unclear whether a probe trained on one open model's activations transfers to another family. There is no benchmark measuring cross-family probe transfer.

**Direction:** Train simple logistic-regression probes on residual-stream activations (collected with hooks) for jailbroken vs benign prompts on one open model (e.g., Llama-3-8B), then evaluate the SAME probe (after aligning hidden dims via a learned linear map or shared-direction projection) on Qwen, Mistral, Gemma. Report a transfer matrix of detection AUC.

**Why it matters:** If probes transfer, small labs can reuse detectors instead of retraining per model; if they don't, that's a critical caveat for cheap-monitor deployment. Recent work shows refusal directions align across the Llama-Qwen-Mistral-Phi cluster, making transfer plausible and worth measuring. Single GPU, no training of LLMs.

**Relevant context:** Arditi et al. 'Refusal in LMs Is Mediated by a Single Direction' (NeurIPS 2024); 'Jailbreak Transferability Emerges from Shared Representations' (arXiv:2506.12913) finds same-axis directions align tightly across LQMP cluster. Anthropic 'Cost-Effective Constitutional Classifiers via Representation Re-use' (alignment.anthropic.com 2025). Context file: 'replicate on different model families.'

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: cross-family probe transfer determines whether cheap jailbreak monitors are reusable, bearing on deployment robustness.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: hook-based activation extraction plus cross-family hidden-dim alignment needs solid ML fundamentals.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused transfer matrix deliverable; dim-alignment across families adds a modest workstream.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: open models, single GPU, reusable-detector benchmark labs underprioritize.

low_compute.reasoning: Activation extraction + logistic probes; single GPU, no LLM training.

novelty.reasoning: Refusal-direction transfer is studied; a cross-family probe-transfer benchmark may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Shared refusal directions are documented; a standardized cross-family probe-transfer benchmark is the open angle.
